home-remodeling.local_heading: The isles are not ordinary lots
intro_paragraphs: Las Olas Isles came out of a dredge in the 1920s, when Fort Lauderdale decided it wanted to be the Venice of America and cut finger islands into the mangrove. Almost none of the original bungalows survive. What stands today on Nurmi Isles, Hendricks Isle, Isle of Venice and Seven Isles is a mix: 1950s and 1960s waterfront ranches, Mediterranean Revival rebuilds, Key West-style two-stories, and glass-and-limestone contemporaries from the last fifteen years. Whole-home remodeling here usually means gutting a mid-century house down to its block shell and rebuilding around the water view.

Fort Lauderdale Development Services handles the permit, and since the city went paperless, submittals go up through LauderBuild rather than across a counter. Broward adds a layer above the city: the county Board of Rules and Appeals publishes the Broward amendments to the Florida Building Code, certifies the building officials and inspectors who will review your job, and issues the formal interpretations that settle arguments. Broward sits in the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, so every window, door and skylight needs product approval valid for the HVHZ. On these isles, FEMA flood rules and the fifty percent substantial-improvement threshold shape how far a gut can go.

The crew doing it has been building in South Florida for more than twenty years, with 150-plus remodels and additions delivered, all of them permitted and inspected. On a Las Olas isle that experience shows up as logistics: one lane in, one lane out, neighbors close enough to hear the saw, and a dock that may be the only sane way to land material. We scope the whole job in writing before demolition, keep a supervisor on site every working day, protect what stays, and hand you one accountable team from estimate through warranty.

scope_items.name: New service, new stacks
scope_items.desc: Replacement electrical service and panels, repiped supply and drain lines, and ducted systems sized for a house that now runs on glass and appliances.

scope_items.name: Slab, block and levels
scope_items.desc: Floor level corrections, slab repair where fill has settled near the seawall, and block work that turns a 1962 layout into one open plan.

scope_items.name: Finishes and millwork
scope_items.desc: Custom cabinetry, stone, interior doors and closets built to the drawings rather than the catalog, installed after the wet trades have finished and dried.

faqs.q: Who issues the permit for a whole-home remodel on Las Olas Isles?
faqs.a: The City of Fort Lauderdale does, through its Development Services Department and Building Services Division. Applications and plans are submitted digitally through LauderBuild; paper sets are no longer accepted. Behind the city sits the Broward County Board of Rules and Appeals, which certifies the officials and inspectors reviewing your project and publishes the Broward amendments to the Florida Building Code. Miami-Dade's building department has no role on this side of the county line.

faqs.q: Will the fifty percent FEMA rule stop me from gutting the house?
faqs.a: It might redirect the project rather than stop it. On isle lots in a special flood hazard area, if the cost of improvements reaches half the structure's pre-improvement market value, the whole building has to be brought into current flood compliance. Because the threshold can accumulate across permits, we look at it before design, not at plan review. Sometimes the honest read is that a rebuild beats a gut, and we will say so.

faqs.q: Is there an architectural review board I have to satisfy here?
faqs.a: Not the way some South Florida cities work. Las Olas Isles is not a designated historic district, and Fort Lauderdale's Historic Preservation Board reviews exterior work in districts like Sailboat Bend, not on the isles. What you do answer to is zoning: setbacks, lot coverage, height and the waterway rules in the city's Unified Land Development Regulations. The Las Olas Isles Homeowners Association is a voluntary neighborhood group, not a permit authority.

faqs.q: How long does a full gut take on the isles?
faqs.a: Plan in seasons. Design and engineering typically take a few months, city review adds more depending on how complete the submittal is, and construction on a full house commonly runs most of a year. Waterfront jobs stretch when seawall, dock or flood work joins the scope, since county environmental licensing runs on its own clock. You get a written schedule with the estimate, and daily supervision is how we defend it.

faqs.q: What should a whole-home remodel here cost?
faqs.a: Wide range, and anyone who answers in one number has not looked at your house. A finish-level refresh and a structural gut with new mechanicals and impact openings are different projects with different budgets. What we commit to is a fixed written scope with real allowances, so the number you sign is the number you pay unless something genuinely unforeseen turns up and gets documented. PGX competes on certainty and finish, not on being the low bid.

kitchen-remodeling.title: Kitchen Remodeling, Las Olas Isles FL | PGX Builders
kitchen-remodeling.meta_description: Las Olas Isles kitchen remodeling in Fort Lauderdale, FL. We move the kitchen to the canal side, cabinetry and stone included. (786) 273-2524.
kitchen-remodeling.hero_sub: Custom cabinetry, stone and layout changes for Las Olas Isles kitchens, with appliances relocated, lighting designed and structure engineered, permitted through Fort Lauderdale and run by a licensed general contractor who is on site daily.
intro_paragraphs: Ask an owner on Isle of Capri or Bontona Avenue what is wrong with the kitchen and the answer is rarely the countertop. It is the wall. Waterfront houses built here in the 1950s and 1960s put the kitchen at the front of the plan, facing the street, with the canal reserved for the living room and a Florida room nobody uses. High-end kitchen remodeling on the Las Olas Isles is mostly a relocation project: pulling the kitchen toward the water, absorbing a utility room, and putting an island where the view actually is.

A kitchen that moves takes plumbing, gas, electrical and often structure with it, so it is a permitted job through Fort Lauderdale Development Services with inspections at rough and final. Enlarging the window over the sink or cutting a new opening to the terrace brings the exterior into play, which means units carrying product approval valid in the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone that includes Broward County. Older isle houses frequently need a service upgrade before they can carry an induction range, a wine room and a pair of dishwashers, and that work rides on the same permit set.

Our sequence is the one cabinetmakers ask for and rarely get: structure first, then rough-ins verified against the shop drawings, cabinets set and leveled, stone templated on the actual boxes. Cabinet lead times drive the calendar, so we order early and hold demolition until the delivery date is real. A supervisor is on site each working day, the rest of the house is sealed off and protected, and the scope is fixed in writing before a single wall opens. Twenty-plus years and 150-plus projects in South Florida, all permitted and inspected, sit behind that.
kitchen-remodeling.scope_heading: What goes into an isle kitchen
kitchen-remodeling.scope_intro: Priced line by line before demolition, never guessed at afterward. These five elements carry most Las Olas Isles kitchen projects.

scope_items.name: Moving the kitchen
scope_items.desc: Relocating the whole room toward the canal side, with drains, gas and vent runs redesigned rather than stretched from wherever the 1958 plumber left them.

scope_items.name: Cabinetry with no filler strips
scope_items.desc: Shop-drawn cabinet packages with finishes chosen to survive humidity and salt air, scaled to your ceilings instead of the nearest stock dimension.

scope_items.name: Slab stone on islands
scope_items.desc: Marble, quartzite or porcelain slabs templated after the boxes are set, with island framing and overhang supports sized for the weight they carry.

scope_items.name: Structural openings
scope_items.desc: Beams and columns where a bearing wall between kitchen and living room has to disappear, engineered and sealed before the permit is even filed.

scope_items.name: Power, light and air
scope_items.desc: Panel and service upgrades, dedicated circuits for the appliance package, make-up air for a serious hood, and lighting layered for cooking and for evenings.

faqs.q: Can the kitchen be moved to the canal side of the house?
faqs.a: Usually, and it is the single change that transforms these houses. Drain lines have to be rerouted with proper fall, which on a slab means cutting and repouring, and gas and vent paths need a route that works. Structure is the other question: the wall you want gone may be carrying roof load, so an engineer sizes the beam before we price the job. It is not a weekend decision, but it is the right one.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for a kitchen remodel in Fort Lauderdale?
faqs.a: For a real one, yes. Plumbing, gas, electrical and structural work all require permits through the city's Building Services Division, submitted through LauderBuild, with inspections before anything gets closed up. Cabinet swaps into existing hookups and paint do not. Skipping permits catches up with isle owners at resale, when the buyer's inspector notices a kitchen that does not appear in the property's permit history and the closing slows down.

faqs.q: Will a bigger window over the sink trigger extra review?
faqs.a: It changes the permit, not the politics. There is no architectural board reviewing single-family exteriors on the isles, but a new or enlarged opening becomes a structural and product-approval item: a header sized by the engineer and a unit approved for the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone that covers Broward County. If the house sits in a flood zone, the cost of the work also counts toward the substantial-improvement calculation. We flag both at the walk-through.

faqs.q: How long will we be without a kitchen?
faqs.a: Longer than the demolition suggests and shorter than it feels. Custom cabinetry is fabricated in months, not weeks, so we sequence around the delivery date instead of tearing out early and staring at a hole. On-site construction for a full kitchen commonly runs a couple of months, more when structure or relocation is involved. Most clients set up a temporary kitchen in the garage or the Florida room and survive it.

faqs.q: What drives the budget on a high-end kitchen here?
faqs.a: Cabinetry and stone, then appliances, then whatever the house hides. Moving the room adds slab work and rerouted services; a service upgrade adds a panel and utility coordination. Selections move the number more than square footage does. We price against a written specification after walking the space, so you are comparing a real scope rather than a per-foot guess. We are rarely the lowest bid and are usually the clearest one.

kitchen-remodeling.cta_sub: Twenty minutes in the room and we can tell you what moves, what stays, and what it takes, in English o en español.

bathroom-remodeling.title: Bathroom Remodeling in Las Olas Isles, FL | PGX Builders
bathroom-remodeling.meta_description: Bathroom and primary suite remodeling on the Las Olas Isles, Fort Lauderdale FL. Flood-tested waterproofing, stone, frameless glass. Call (786) 273-2524.
bathroom-remodeling.hero_sub: Primary suites, frameless showers and freestanding tubs for Las Olas Isles homes, with waterproofing flood-tested before tile and every trade permitted and inspected under a licensed Fort Lauderdale general contractor.
bathroom-remodeling.local_heading: Salt air is hard on bathrooms
intro_paragraphs: The bathrooms are usually the last honest thing left in a Las Olas Isles house. A 1961 waterfront home on Hendricks Isle or San Marco Drive came with a compact hall bath, a slightly larger one off the primary bedroom, and no concept of a suite. Even the 1990s renovations are dated now: framed shower doors, a garden tub nobody has filled in a decade, a vanity built for one. Owners here combine a bedroom or a closet into the primary bath and rebuild it properly in stone and glass.

Bathroom work is permitted through Fort Lauderdale Development Services, with plumbing, electrical and mechanical inspections along the way, and those inspections are the reason the waterproofing gets verified before tile hides it. Broward inspectors are certified by the county Board of Rules and Appeals and work from the Broward amendments to the Florida Building Code, so expect a reviewer who knows exactly what a shower pan detail should look like. On these isles the deeper issue is age: cast iron drains and galvanized supply from the original build, and slabs poured on dredge fill.

A bathroom is a small building with no tolerance for optimism. Membranes get flood-tested and held overnight before anyone sets tile, slopes get confirmed with a level, blocking goes in behind the walls for heavy glass and grab bars whether or not you want them yet, and fixtures near salt air get specified for it. Fixed written scope, daily supervision, protected floors between the front door and the work, licensed and insured under Lic. CGC1539072. Water finds the one detail you skipped.
bathroom-remodeling.scope_heading: Building a bath on the isles
bathroom-remodeling.scope_intro: Every bathroom is drawn, specified and priced before the first tile order goes out. The work below covers most isle primary suites and guest baths.

scope_items.name: Suites carved from bedrooms
scope_items.desc: Reworking an adjacent bedroom, hallway or closet into a real primary bath and dressing area, with plans, rough-ins and permits handled as one package.

scope_items.name: Flood-tested waterproofing
scope_items.desc: Bonded membranes, curbs and pans tested with standing water and signed off before tile, because retiling a failed shower costs more than doing it once.

scope_items.name: Curbless where the slab allows
scope_items.desc: Recessed pans and linear drains cut into the slab where the structure and drain fall allow, with an honest low-curb alternative when they do not.

scope_items.name: New lines behind open walls
scope_items.desc: Swapping original cast iron and galvanized runs for new drain and supply lines while the walls are already open and access costs nothing extra.

scope_items.name: Stone, glass and hardware
scope_items.desc: Marble and quartzite sealed for daily use, heavy frameless glass hung on real blocking, and finishes chosen to hold up near a saltwater canal.

faqs.q: Is a permit required to redo a bathroom in Fort Lauderdale?
faqs.a: Yes, for anything past paint and a mirror. Relocating or replacing plumbing, changing electrical, adding an exhaust fan or altering framing all go through the city's Building Services Division for permit and inspection. That is genuinely in your favor here: a Broward-certified inspector looks at the rough plumbing and the waterproofing while they are still visible, and the permit record follows the house to closing.

faqs.q: Our drains are original cast iron. Replace them or leave them?
faqs.a: If the walls and floor are opening anyway, replace them. Cast iron from the 1950s and 1960s is at the end of its useful life, and isle houses sit low, so a slow or root-invaded line shows up as a smell before it shows up as a backup. We camera the lines early so the decision rests on footage rather than instinct, and we do the work while access is free.

faqs.q: Does bathroom work count toward the FEMA fifty percent rule?
faqs.a: It can. On a property in a special flood hazard area, improvement costs are measured against the building's market value, and jurisdictions may look at permits cumulatively over a period rather than one at a time. A single guest bath rarely moves the needle; three bathrooms, a kitchen and a roof in the same stretch might. Fort Lauderdale's floodplain staff maintains elevation certificates and can confirm your property's status before you design.

faqs.q: Why do fixtures corrode faster on the isles?
faqs.a: Because you live on saltwater. Homes on Nurmi Isles or Isle of Palms sit feet from a tidal canal, and airborne salt reaches hardware, hinges, shower door tracks and exhaust grilles even with the windows shut. Polished chrome and solid brass generally hold up, some finishes and coatings do not, and cheap glass hardware pits within a couple of seasons. We specify for the environment and tell you which finish is a maintenance commitment.

faqs.q: What does a primary bath at this level run?
faqs.a: It is set by three things: the size of the footprint change, the stone and glass package, and how much plumbing has to be rebuilt behind the walls. That last one is where budgets get surprised, and it is why we open exploratory access and camera the drains before quoting rather than after. You get a fixed written number against a specification. We build to a standard first and price it honestly second.

bathroom-remodeling.cta_sub: Show us the room and the reference photos. You will get a real scope, a real schedule and a real number, in English o en español.

home-additions.meta_description: Adding on to a finger island: second stories, rear extensions and ground-floor suites engineered for HVHZ on the Las Olas Isles. (786) 273-2524.
home-additions.h1: Adding on to a finger island
home-additions.hero_sub: Rear extensions, second stories and garage conversions for Las Olas Isles homes, engineered for HVHZ wind loads, checked against flood and setback rules, permitted through Fort Lauderdale and supervised daily.
home-additions.local_heading: Room to grow, on a narrow lot
intro_paragraphs: Las Olas Isles lots are long and narrow by design. The dredge cut them that way in the 1920s to maximize water frontage, which is wonderful for dockage and unforgiving for square footage. So additions on Coral Way, Riviera Isles or Royal Palm Drive tend to go up rather than out: a second story over a 1950s ranch, a primary suite above the garage, a rear extension squeezed between the side setbacks. Multigenerational households add ground-floor suites. Owners who love the street and the water build instead of moving.

Fort Lauderdale's Unified Land Development Regulations get specific about additions: setbacks, lot coverage, height and yard requirements for your zoning district, all reviewed by Development Services before the building permit issues. Structural engineering is not optional, since a second story means proving the existing block walls and footings can take it, and everything new must meet High-Velocity Hurricane Zone requirements under the Broward amendments to the Florida Building Code. Flood elevation matters too: an addition in a special flood hazard area has its own elevation and substantial-improvement math.

Twenty-plus years in South Florida and 150-plus remodels and additions have taught us where the money and the schedule hide: tying a new foundation to an old one on fill, matching stucco and roof so the seam disappears, and keeping half a house livable while the other half is scaffolded. Access on an isle is a project of its own, since a crane, a concrete pump and a lumber delivery all have to fit on one lane without blocking your neighbors. We plan that before we mobilize.
home-additions.scope_heading: Adding on to an isle house
home-additions.scope_intro: Each of these starts with a survey, a structural engineer and a hard look at what the zoning district allows on your particular lot.

scope_items.name: Going up over the block
scope_items.desc: Adding a full upper floor once the engineer confirms the existing walls and footings can carry it, with reinforcement designed in where they cannot.

scope_items.name: Pushing out toward the canal
scope_items.desc: Living space extended within the setbacks, with new footings, tie-beams and roof tie-ins detailed so the addition never reads as bolted on.

scope_items.name: Garage and carport conversions
scope_items.desc: Turning covered parking into conditioned rooms, insulated and mechanically served, permitted properly so the appraiser can count the space.

scope_items.name: Ground-floor family suites
scope_items.desc: Ground-level quarters with a shower bath and compact galley for family or crew, permitted properly and scaled so they belong to the original house.

scope_items.name: Foundations on fill
scope_items.desc: Footings, underpinning and tie-beam upgrades designed for soil that was dredged into place a century ago, which is the half of the budget nobody photographs.

faqs.q: Will a second story fly on a Las Olas Isles lot?
faqs.a: Often yes, and an engineer answers it, not a salesperson. The existing block walls, tie-beam and footings get evaluated first; where they fall short, columns, reinforcement or new footings are designed in. Zoning then sets the ceiling through height limits, setbacks and lot coverage for your district. Occasionally the honest conclusion is that a rear extension gives you more usable space for less money, and we will put both options in front of you.

faqs.q: How close to the seawall can an addition go?
faqs.a: Not as close as most owners hope. Fort Lauderdale sets a rear yard requirement measured from the property line at the water, and the seawall itself has to stay accessible for inspection, maintenance and eventual replacement. Building right up against an aging wall is how a straightforward seawall job later becomes a demolition job. We survey the line, check the setback for your zoning district, and design with room to work behind the addition.

faqs.q: What is the realistic timeline from first meeting to finished addition?
faqs.a: Front-load your patience. Survey, design, structural engineering and permitting through Fort Lauderdale Development Services routinely fill several months before ground breaks, longer when flood compliance or a variance enters the picture. Construction of a substantial addition then runs several more months, and a full second story generally means a year-scale commitment. We publish the whole timeline in writing with the estimate so no phase arrives as a surprise.

faqs.q: Can we stay in the house while you build the addition?
faqs.a: Usually yes for a rear extension, rarely for a second story. Extensions can be sealed off behind temporary walls with their own access, and most families live around them. Going up means opening the roof, relocating mechanicals and living under scaffolding, which is bearable for a few weeks and grim for six months. We map the disruption honestly at the estimate stage so you can decide about a rental before demolition, not during it.

faqs.q: Does adding on beat buying a bigger house on the isles?
faqs.a: It depends on what you are attached to. If the dockage, the canal and the walk to Las Olas Boulevard are the reason you bought, an addition buys the space without giving up any of that or resetting your tax basis. If the lot is already tight against setbacks, or the structure needs more help than it is worth, moving may win. We give a candid feasibility read before anyone pays for drawings.

outdoor-living.h1: The dock is the front yard
outdoor-living.hero_sub: Summer kitchens, pool terraces, pergolas and dock-side decks for Las Olas Isles homes, coordinated with city permits and Broward County environmental licensing and built by a licensed, insured general contractor.
outdoor-living.local_heading: Where the house meets the canal
intro_paragraphs: On the isles the backyard has a boat in it. Every one of these lots has water frontage and, because there are no fixed bridges between here and the Port Everglades inlet, that frontage can hold serious vessels. So outdoor living across the Las Olas Isles, from Seven Isles to Idlewyld and Coconut Isle, is organized around the dock: a covered terrace facing the canal, a summer kitchen that serves the boat as much as the pool, shade structures that survive a Fort Lauderdale August, and hardscape that connects the two.

Exterior work here crosses more desks than interior work. Structures, gas, water and electrical are permitted through Fort Lauderdale Development Services. Anything in or over the water, meaning docks, boat lifts and seawall repair, also needs a Broward County environmental license, and often state and federal review as well. The city's Unified Land Development Regulations limit how far a dock may project into the waterway, generally a percentage of the waterway width or twenty-five feet, whichever is less. Fort Lauderdale has also adopted the regional five-foot NAVD88 seawall standard, so a major seawall repair can trigger raising the whole wall.

PGX builds exteriors to interior standards and stays in its lane on the water. Summer kitchen gas, water and power get permitted and inspected; pergola footings are engineered for HVHZ wind loads; terraces are pitched to drain away from the house instead of toward the slider. When a project also involves the dock or the seawall, we coordinate with the marine contractor and the county licensing rather than pretend it is one trade. Fixed written scope, a supervisor on site daily, a clean site every evening.
outdoor-living.scope_intro: Terraces, summer kitchens, driveways and facades, designed and permitted as one project so the trades are not arguing over the same square of concrete.

scope_items.name: Summer kitchens near saltwater
scope_items.desc: A cooking wall on permitted gas, water and power, in marine-grade stainless with stone sealed for a canal that breathes salt all day.

scope_items.name: Shade that stays put
scope_items.desc: Loggias and pergolas anchored into real footings, with hurricane-zone connection hardware and proportions taken from the house rather than the catalog page.

scope_items.name: Pool decks and hardscape
scope_items.desc: Coping, pavers and finished concrete laid with real drainage between the pool, the terrace and the seawall walkway, so nothing ponds after an afternoon storm.

scope_items.name: Driveways and street presence
scope_items.desc: Motor courts, aprons and walkways rebuilt for the narrow isle frontage, with permits for work touching the right-of-way handled before the saw cuts anything.

scope_items.name: Facade, coatings and sliders
scope_items.desc: Exterior restoration, elastomeric coatings that hold against wind-driven rain, and replacement of sliders and terrace doors with HVHZ-approved impact units.

faqs.q: Who permits a dock or seawall project on Las Olas Isles?
faqs.a: More than one agency. The City of Fort Lauderdale permits the structure, Broward County's environmental permitting division issues the license for work in or over the water, and depending on scope the state and the Army Corps may weigh in. Timelines are set by whichever review is slowest, not by the construction. We coordinate the upland work with your marine contractor so the terrace and the dock arrive on the same schedule.

faqs.q: How far can my dock extend into the canal?
faqs.a: Less far than most people assume. Fort Lauderdale's land development regulations cap mooring structures at twenty-five percent of the waterway width or twenty-five feet from the property line, whichever is smaller, with a separate allowance for mooring piles, and a vessel is not supposed to extend past your side setbacks projected into the water. No variance gets you past the code's outer limit on waterway width. Check the numbers against your canal before you order steel.

faqs.q: Do pergolas and summer kitchens really need permits?
faqs.a: They do. A shade structure is a structure, and in Broward it has to be engineered and inspected for High-Velocity Hurricane Zone wind loads, because an unpermitted pergola becomes airborne debris in September. Gas, water and electrical for an outdoor kitchen each carry their own trade permits and inspections. It is more paperwork than a grill island looks like it deserves, and it is also what stands between your terrace and your insurance carrier.

faqs.q: How do you get materials onto a one-lane isle without a war?
faqs.a: Planning and warning. Deliveries get scheduled rather than dumped, concrete pours are booked for the quietest window we can get, and the crew parks where the city and your neighbors can live with it. On tighter isles we stage material in phases instead of filling the swale for a month, and occasionally the water is the better road. Fort Lauderdale's noise and work-hour rules apply, and we keep the site swept at the end of every day.

faqs.q: What does a full outdoor living build usually involve financially?
faqs.a: It scales with utilities and structure more than with area. A paver terrace and drainage is one conversation; a covered outdoor room with a summer kitchen, gas, water, power and lighting is a different one, and appliance and stone selections swing it further. Anything touching the seawall or dock brings a second permitting track and its own cost. We walk the yard, write the specification, and price against that rather than a per-foot rule of thumb.

A dock on Hendricks Isle was rebuilt with nothing in the file. A Florida room on Isle of Venice was enclosed one weekend in the 1970s and never mentioned again. Waterfront records run long here, and canal-side work has always been the easiest to do quietly. The other half of these calls come from owners planning real work who want it filed correctly the first time.

The permit is a City of Fort Lauderdale matter, filed with Development Services and its Building Services Division through LauderBuild. Behind it sits the county layer: the Broward County Board of Rules and Appeals, which certifies every building official and inspector who will touch your file, keeps the county amendments to the Florida Building Code current, hears the appeals and writes the interpretations that end code arguments. Broward is High-Velocity Hurricane Zone territory, so glass, doors and roofing need approvals valid for the HVHZ, and on a flood-zone isle lot the substantial improvement threshold shapes how much you can do at once.

PGX Builders Group is the licensed general contractor whose name goes on the permit, Lic. CGC1539072, not a paperwork broker, so the responsibility comes with the application. We bring in the architect, engineer or surveyor a complete file actually requires, answer plan-review comments in one round instead of three, and have a supervisor on site when the inspector arrives, which on a one-lane isle matters more than it sounds. Twenty-plus years in South Florida and 150-plus remodels and additions, every one permitted and inspected, taught us that a job is not finished when the paint dries. It is finished when the file reads closed.
permitting-compliance.scope_heading: From application to a closed file
permitting-compliance.scope_intro: Filed ahead of a remodel or opened up years after the fact, these five fronts decide whether an isle property reads clean on paper.

scope_items.name: Permits left without a final
scope_items.desc: We pull the address history at the city, establish what each open record still owes, and carry it through re-inspection, revision or a replacement permit.

scope_items.name: Seawall, dock and lift filings
scope_items.desc: Waterfront structures permitted properly, with the county environmental review that canal work triggers coordinated alongside the city permit instead of discovered halfway through.

scope_items.name: Approved openings, documented
scope_items.desc: Windows, doors and roofing matched to approvals valid inside the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, with anchor details and installation instructions in the set before anything ships.

scope_items.name: Inspections called in sequence
scope_items.desc: Phased inspections requested when the work is genuinely ready and met on site by a supervisor, because a re-inspection on a one-lane island costs a week.

scope_items.name: Legalizing unpermitted work
scope_items.desc: Enclosed carports, added baths, swapped glass and rebuilt docks brought back through as-built drawings, engineering and inspection against the code in force today.

faqs.q: We close in six weeks and title found an open permit. Can it still be cleared?
faqs.a: Often, and the sooner you start the better. We pull the file from the city, read what each open record is actually missing, and sort it: some need only the final inspection nobody ever called, some need a revision or a letter from an engineer, and work done with no permit may need one after the fact plus construction opened up where an inspector can see it. Fort Lauderdale closes a permit by inspecting it, so this is real work rather than a phone call.

faqs.q: Do I file with the city or with Broward County?
faqs.a: With the city. Fort Lauderdale reviews, issues and inspects residential permits through Development Services, and the submittal goes up digitally on LauderBuild. Broward County's role is different and easy to misread: the Board of Rules and Appeals sets the code framework the city enforces and certifies the people enforcing it, but you do not file there. Separately, work in the waterway brings county environmental licensing into the picture, which is its own application on its own schedule.

faqs.q: Does a seawall, dock or boat lift need a permit?
faqs.a: Every one of them. Seawall caps and panels, dock decking and pilings, davits and lifts are permitted structures, and because they sit in or over the water they usually add Broward County environmental licensing, with state or federal review on larger scopes. This is also the most common unpermitted finding on the isles, since the work arrives by barge and leaves no trace on the street. Expect it to run on its own clock, and start well before you want the boat back.

faqs.q: Our building has a milestone inspection coming. Can PGX do the repairs?
faqs.a: Yes, once the report exists. Florida's milestone inspection and structural integrity reserve study requirements reach condominium and cooperative buildings of three habitable stories and up, which covers the low-rise buildings rather than the single-family houses that make up most of the isles. The inspection itself is signed by a Florida-licensed engineer or architect the association retains, and that is not our role. What we take on is the repair scope it produces: concrete restoration, waterproofing, balcony and railing work, electrical corrections, permitted and inspected.

faqs.q: How long does plan review take, and what does permitting add to the budget?
faqs.a: Weeks rather than days, and the honest variable is how complete the first submittal is. Interior work with no structural change moves quickest. Anything carrying sealed engineering, flood compliance or waterway review takes longer, because those approvals run in sequence rather than side by side. Fees are set by the jurisdiction and scale with the value of the work, so we quote them against your real scope instead of inventing a figure here. We price the whole path to a closed permit, not the part that ends at demolition.

permitting-compliance.cta_sub: Send the address and whatever the title search turned up. You get a straight read on where you stand and the fix in writing, in English o en español.
